sections.title: In, on, or at — Hungarian keeps them apart
sections.content: Hungarian has three different static-location suffixes where English gets by with just "in/on/at". -ban/-ben is for anything inside a container or room. -on/-en/-ön is for anything resting on a surface. -nál/-nél is for being near a person or a specific place. Picking the right one is about the real relationship between the object and the place — not about translating word for word.

sections.title: Which one do I need?
rows: on a surface — a szőnyegen (on the rug)
at someone's — a szomszédnál (at the neighbor's)

items.english: The key is in the drawer.
The shoes are on the rug.

sections.content: -nál/-nél is the odd one out here — you already met it for people and places (a szomszédnál, Máriannál), never for a plain object. A key or a book is never nál/nél anything; only a person, a shop, or a place can be.
